nodes.description: Germline SLC30A2 variants in the mother inactivate ZnT2, the zinc transporter that loads zinc into the secretory vesicles of lactating mammary epithelial cells. Missense alleles act in two ways. H54R and G87R mutants are retained in the endoplasmic reticulum or aggregate perinuclearly and are unstable, and G87R also pulls wild-type ZnT2 into nonfunctional dimers (dominant negative). G280R, T312M and E355Q hit residues for zinc coordination or permeation, still reach vesicles and do not inhibit the wild-type protein, implying haploinsufficiency. Splice-altering and promoter variants have also been reported. A single heterozygous allele usually suffices; compound heterozygous (W152R with S296L) and homozygous (E88K) mothers have also been described, the latter with earlier onset in the infant.
